turns.learner: Hello teacher! I want to practise understanding unknown words when I read a story.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Great, let's practise. When you see a new word, look at the words and sentences around it. They give you clues.

Example: "The crowd was huge; thousands of people filled the street." Huge means very big. The clue is "thousands of people."

Now you try. "It rained all week and nobody visited. Joe sat alone at the window, feeling miserable." What does "miserable" mean? A) very happy B) very sad C) very fast. Reply with the letter only.

Yes, B is right! Miserable means very sad. Which clues helped you? Look again: "rained all week", "nobody visited", "sat alone".

Next one. "The teacher was fair. She gave every student the same time and the same rules." What does "fair" mean? A) a funfair B) light in colour C) treating everyone the same. Reply with the letter only.

Not quite. "Fair" can mean a funfair, but let's test it in the sentence: "The teacher was a funfair. She gave every student the same time." That does not make sense.

Look at the clue: "the same time and the same rules." What does that tell you about the teacher? Try again: A, B or C?

turns.learner: Oh, the teacher is not a funfair. Maybe C, treating everyone the same?
turns.tutor:
Yes, C is right! Fair here means treating everyone the same. You tested the meaning in the sentence, and that is a great way to check.

Words can have more than one meaning. Try a new one: "Ali has fair hair, so he wears a hat in the sun." What does "fair" mean here? What is the clue?

turns.learner: Fair is treating everyone the same, I think. Maybe his hair is the same as other people?
turns.tutor:
Good try, but let's test it. "Ali has treating-everyone-the-same hair" does not make sense, right?

Look at the clue: "he wears a hat in the sun." Light skin and light hair burn easily in the sun. So "fair hair" means light in colour. Same word, different meaning! Now test it: "Ali has light-colour hair, so he wears a hat." Does that make sense?

turns.learner: Yes, that makes sense. So fair can be light colour too. Different sentence, different meaning?
turns.tutor:
Exactly! Different sentence, different meaning. The words around the word are the context, and they give you clues. Then test your meaning in the sentence.

One more: "We went to the fair and rode the big wheel." What does "fair" mean here? Tell me the clue you used.

turns.learner: Fair is a funfair here. The clue is big wheel, because funfair has big wheel.
turns.tutor:
Perfect! "Big wheel" is a great clue, and funfair makes sense in the sentence. You found three meanings of "fair" today: fair play, light colour, and funfair.

Remember the steps: 1) read the words around it, 2) find a clue, 3) test the meaning in the sentence. Well done!
